objectives.label: Present indicative for a current fact
objectives.description: Choose and interpret a present-indicative form that states a current fact. This objective excludes the historical temporal use of haber.

review.reason: Scope is limited to an explicit current fact and matches the cited present-indicative leaf.

objectives.label: Temporal ha in older Spanish
objectives.description: Interpret temporal ha plus a duration as locating an event that amount of time in the past, including no ha mucho tiempo as not long ago. This objective excludes ordinary present-tense and compound-perfect uses of haber.

review.reason: RAE haber section 4.2 confirms the surviving temporal use; the scope is separate from ordinary present forms.

objectives.label: Imperfect for background and habit
objectives.description: Interpret an imperfect verb as an ongoing background state or a repeated past habit when context supports that reading. Assessment does not cover every contrast between the imperfect and preterite.

review.reason: The objective distinguishes ongoing background and repeated past readings without claiming the whole preterite contrast.

objectives.label: Scope of no
objectives.description: Identify the verb or expression negated by no in a short clause, such as no quiero acordarme. Historical temporal haber is assessed separately.

review.reason: The revised scope tests one explicit negated expression and no longer conflates it with temporal haber.

objectives.label: Articles and noun-phrase agreement
objectives.description: Match an article or descriptive adjective to its noun by gender and number in a simple noun phrase. Assessment excludes verb agreement and agreement across long-distance ellipsis.

review.reason: Gender and number agreement in short noun phrases is narrow, observable, and aligned to the cited leaves.

objectives.label: Acordarse de
objectives.description: Use and interpret acordarse de as a pronominal verb meaning to remember, including an attached pronoun on an infinitive such as acordarme.

review.reason: The construction and governed de complement are explicit, with attached-pronoun infinitives included in scope.

objectives.label: Possessive relative cuyo
objectives.description: Connect cuyo, cuya, cuyos, or cuyas to an antecedent while making the form agree with the possessed noun. Assessment uses explicit relative clauses with a clear antecedent.

review.reason: The objective separately requires antecedent resolution and agreement with the possessed noun, matching the source construction.

objectives.label: Quantity comparison between nouns
objectives.description: Interpret más plus one noun plus que plus another noun as a comparison between their amounts, as in más vaca que carnero.

review.reason: The objective now covers only comparisons between quantities of two nouns, separate from fractions.

objectives.label: Las tres partes as three quarters
objectives.description: With the annotated opening gloss supplied, interpret las tres partes de su hacienda as three of four parts of the hidalgo's income.

review.reason: CVC opening note 9 supplies the historical three-quarters reading; its evidence is kept separate from general comparison skill.

objectives.label: Weekdays as recurring time
objectives.description: Interpret a plural weekday with the definite article, such as los sábados, as a recurring habit rather than one dated event.

review.reason: The form and recurring-time interpretation are explicit and do not claim mastery of other weekday expressions.

objectives.label: Pronominal se with the subject
objectives.description: Interpret se when a named subject performs an action involving or presenting that same subject, as in se honraba or se viste. Assessment excludes passive and impersonal se.

review.reason: The scope is limited to identifying the named subject of a transparent pronominal construction, excluding passive and impersonal se.

objectives.label: Hidalgo in the opening

lessons.title: Place, memory, and the opening time frame
lessons.readingGoal: Understand why the narrator withholds the place name and place the hidalgo's life in the past.
lessons.explanation: The opening moves through a relative clause before reaching its main past description. In de cuyo nombre no quiero acordarme, cuyo connects nombre to lugar, no negates quiero, and acordarme uses the complement de, moved before cuyo. The phrase no ha mucho tiempo means not long ago in this older temporal use of haber; vivía then supplies the continuing past background.

review.reason: Independent exact-version review: teaching, examples and source support the reviewed clue and distinct acordarse message check; scoped near transfer does not establish learning efficacy.

lessons.title: Meals, weekly habits, and household means
lessons.readingGoal: Follow the long food list and understand what it says about the hidalgo's recurring expenses.
lessons.explanation: The foods form a long plural subject whose verb, consumían, appears near the end. The imperfect presents a customary expense. Los sábados, los viernes, and los domingos describe a weekly routine. Algo más vaca que carnero compares amounts of foods, and las tres partes de su hacienda is glossed here as three quarters of his income.

lessons.title: Clothing, reference, and self-presentation
lessons.readingGoal: Recover who spends the remaining income, what the clothes are, and how the hidalgo presents himself on weekdays.
lessons.explanation: El resto della points back to the hacienda in the previous sentence; della is the older written form de ella. Reading concluían here as used up, its plural ending agrees with the clothing list that follows, so the clothes are the subject and el resto della is the fronted object. A sayo is a garment, while velarte is the cloth used for it. After y, the understood subject changes back to the hidalgo: se honraba describes his self-presentation. Articles and adjectives in a short noun phrase must match the noun's gender and number.

review.reason: Independent exact-version review: historical self-presentation remains accurate; revised relation question and unfamiliar se-deletion comparison align with objective v1 and its exclusions.

questions.explanation: Here se honraba describes the hidalgo’s own respectable self-presentation in his vellorí. It does not describe him presenting another person.

review.reason: Independent exact-version review: exact historical source supports respectable self-presentation; alternatives distinguish participant relations without recasting honrarse as literal dressing.

questions.prompt: Fresh example: A writer changes «Lucía se mira en el espejo» to «Lucía mira en el espejo» by deleting se. (Mirar means to look; espejo means mirror.) Which detail is explicit in the first version but left unstated in the second?

That Lucía is looking in a mirror.
questions.explanation: Se explicitly makes Lucía both the person looking and the person looked at. Without se, the sentence still names Lucía as the subject and the mirror as the setting, but it does not specify whom or what she looks at.

review.reason: Independent exact-version review: deleting se leaves the self-recipient relation unstated while subject, tense and mirror remain; grammatical unique key and editorial comparison differ from placement dressing task.
